unbundled_leads.title: Canonical Ethiopic Ezra and Nehemiah (Ezrâ III), Pereira 1919 — TAU digitized edition lead

entries.mapping_note: The Church page presents ‘Ezra (2nd)’ and ‘Ezra Sutuel’ as one numbered entry. A provisional title-family crosswalk is supported by the Church page's separate statement that the Ethiopic Bible includes third and fourth Esdras, together with TAU's identification of Ethiopic Ezra II with Septuagint Esdras alpha / Vulgate tertius Esdrae and Ezra I (Apocalypse of Esdras) with Vulgate quartus Esdrae. This suggests, but does not prove, that ‘Ezra (2nd)’ corresponds to the third-Esdras work and ‘Ezra Sutuel’ to the fourth-Esdras apocalypse. The British Library codex title names both labels, but its internal boundaries, completeness, exact edition identity, and textual contents are unverified; no reader coverage is claimed. The British Library EAP title lists Ezra Sutu'el, Book of Second Ezra, and an excerpt from the Prayer of the Covenant for one codex; this catalogue title does not establish separate internal boundaries or a complete witness to either Church-list component. The exact work mappings for the Church-list sublabels to the manuscript remain unresolved.

unbundled_leads.title: Te’ezaz section of Ethiopic Sinodos — Horner 1904 image edition
unbundled_leads.scope_description: Cowley reports Te'ezaz as one of four apostolically attributed Sinodos sections, gives a count of 71 or 72 canons, and says it was printed in Horner 1904 (SRC-210). Mikre-Sellassie independently reports 71 canons and cites Horner (SRC-441). Horner's contents identify its English translation of the Ethiopic at printed pp. 127–232 and the Arabic translation beginning at p. 233; these are section locators in Horner's broader Statutes volume, not verified boundaries for Church-list Tizaz. The scan OCR includes headings for Statutes 71 and 72, but the full sequence has not been audited. The linked Internet Archive copy explicitly lacks the Ethiopic and Arabic text witnesses (SRC-368). TAU identifies its external page images as the Te'ezaz section following Horner and reports that printed pages 5, 9, 17, 21, 25, 35, 41, 49, 53, 60, 70, and 71 seem missing in that edition (SRC-213). This is TAU's warning about its hosted edition, not proof that those pages are absent from every witness. Horner's contents identify the English translation of the Ethiopic on pp. 127-232 and the Arabic translation from p. 233; this is a section boundary within Horner's volume, not a verified boundary for the Church-list Tizaz entry. These sources support a strong research association, but this is not an authoritative crosswalk: the modern Church-list spelling/gloss ‘Tizaz (the book of Herald)’ has not been reconciled against a Church text witness; manuscript contents vary, and the 71/72 count differs across reports. Keep the mapping provisional; no text, images, exact boundaries, or reuse permissions are asserted.

The same catalogue distinguishes the separately recorded Apostolic canons (56), CAe 2670. This is a title/work-family discovery lead, not an exact Church-list crosswalk or a single stable text. No text is bundled; completeness and reuse rights are unverified.

unbundled_leads.title: Apostolic canons Abṭelisāt (81) — Beta maṣāḥǝft CAe 2677
unbundled_leads.scope_description: A scholarly work record and manuscript description make this a relevant Abtilis title-family lead, not an exact Church-list crosswalk. Beta records recension differences, including an 80-canon second recension. The separately cataloged 56-canons unit is explicitly distinguished. No witness text or image is bundled, and no completeness or translation claim is made.
unbundled_leads.rights_status: Unresolved. The Beta page shows a file-level CC BY-SA 4.0 statement and site-level CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 notice; their relationship and manuscript-text rights were not determined. No text copied.

unbundled_leads.title: Abtilis / ʿAbṭəlis — reported English Sinodos edition
unbundled_leads.scope_description: The Ethiopian Orthodox Bible Project's 2025-11-05 announcement describes a released English edition of Ethiopic Sinodos and identifies the ʿAbṭəlis section in Horner's 1904 edition. The announcement says the editor uses Horner's 1904 English edition as a basis and compares versions; it does not establish a direct Ge'ez-to-English path for this section. Its placement under the corresponding Church-list title is source-asserted only (Abtilis); the exact published section, boundaries, edition identity, completeness, wording, and relation to a current Church edition have not been independently checked. The linked sales listing and book text were not inspected. No text is bundled.
unbundled_leads.rights_status: Reuse rights for the book text are unknown. The project announcement links to a commercial listing but grants no text-reuse license. No translation text or listing content is reproduced here.

entries.mapping_note: The Church list names I Book of Dominos; the Ethiopian Orthodox Bible Project glosses it as Book of the Covenant I and describes its edition of First Dominos. Beta maṣāḥǝft catalogs the Geʽez Testamentum Domini (CAe 2461), a plausible work-family candidate. The exact Church-list-to-work and edition crosswalk remains uncertain; no text is bundled.

unbundled_leads.title: Testamentum Domini — Geʽez work record CAe 2461
unbundled_leads.scope_description: Plausible work-family candidate for First Book of Dominos based on the Ethiopian Orthodox Bible Project's secondary edition description. The Church-list-to-work crosswalk and identity with any specific printed edition remain unverified.
unbundled_leads.rights_status: No text copied or bundled; rights in the underlying edition and source metadata are not assessed here.

entries.mapping_note: The Church list names II Book of Dominos; the Ethiopian Orthodox Bible Project glosses it as Book of the Covenant II and describes its edition of Second Dominos. Beta maṣāḥǝft catalogs the separate composite Geʽez Testamentum Domini in Galilea (CAe 2462), a plausible work-family candidate. The exact Church-list-to-work and edition crosswalk remains uncertain; no text is bundled.

unbundled_leads.title: Testamentum Domini in Galilea — Geʽez work record CAe 2462
unbundled_leads.scope_description: Plausible work-family candidate for Second Book of Dominos based on the Ethiopian Orthodox Bible Project's secondary edition description. Beta maṣāḥǝft describes a composite: a Galilee apocalypse (chapters 1–11) and the Epistula Apostolorum (chapters 12–62). The Church-list-to-work crosswalk and boundaries in any edition remain unverified.
unbundled_leads.rights_status: No text copied or bundled; rights in the underlying edition and source metadata are not assessed here.

entries.mapping_note: Bausi (2024) identifies the Ethiopic Maṣḥafa Qalemǝnṭos (Book of Clement; CAe 1957) and distinguishes it from the Ethiopic Apocalypse of Peter and from a separate count of three Epistles of Clement. The name overlap makes it a plausible candidate for this English Church-list label, but the Church page gives no Geʽez title and Bausi does not establish this exact list crosswalk. No reader is bundled. A 2024 English print listing titled The Book of Clement from the Ethiopian Bible is a discovery lead (SRC-381). Its bibliographic title and a secondary project’s description as an Ethiopic English version do not independently establish that it translates Bausi’s Maṣḥafa Qalemǝnṭos (CAe 1957) or the exact work intended by this Church-list label. No text is bundled. Fifth Estate separately describes a forthcoming revised reader edition with partial scope (SRC-383); this publisher statement concerns that announced revision and must not be transferred to the distinct 2024 print edition. Publication of the revised edition is unconfirmed. Beta maṣāḥǝft's pinned CAe 1957 TEI record labels Maṣḥafa Qalemǝnṭos / Book of Clement and contains short Geʽez incipits, but no complete reader text. This supports a related-work discovery lead only; it does not establish the exact Church-list crosswalk. Reuse terms conflict across the file and project-level notices (SRC-424, SRC-296, SRC-297).

unbundled_leads.title: Maṣḥafa Qalemǝnṭos (Book of Clement), Eritrean manuscript tradition
unbundled_leads.scope_description: Discovery candidate for Church-list entry eotc-nt-34 (“Book of Clement”) because the scholarly name is also translated “Book of Clement”; the Church list does not give the Geʽez title, so the crosswalk remains uncertain. Bausi describes Qalemǝnṭos as a seven-book Ethiopic work, distinct from the Ethiopic Apocalypse of Peter, only partially corresponding to the Arabic Apocalypse of Peter to Clement. Do not conflate this with the three Epistles of Clement counted together in one broader-canon account (SRC-073), or with the Ethiopic Apocalypse of Peter (CAe 317). No comprehensive critical edition exists; existing French and Italian translations cover different portions. No manuscript images, transcription, or scripture text are bundled.
unbundled_leads.rights_status: The cited scholarly chapter is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; that license applies to the article, not to the Qalemǝnṭos manuscript or translations it discusses. Rights of the witness and French, Italian, and Geʽez–Amharic editions are not established; no text is bundled.

unbundled_leads.title: Maṣḥafa Qalemǝnṭos / Book of Clement — Beta maṣāḥǝft LIT1957Mashaf TEI work record
unbundled_leads.scope_description: Metadata and short text excerpts only: the TEI body contains an introduction, seven numbered Book divisions, and short Geʽez incipit divisions; no continuous, chaptered full-text reader is present in this file. This is a related-work lead for the Church-list ‘Book of Clement’; the exact crosswalk is uncertain. It is not conflated with 1 Clement, 2 Clement, other Clementine works, or the distinct Ethiopic Apocalypse of Peter (CAe 317).
unbundled_leads.rights_status: No transcription is bundled. The pinned TEI file states CC BY-SA 4.0, while current project Guidelines state CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for project data/remixes and the University of Hamburg dataset record gives dataset-level CC BY 4.0 metadata with file-specific terms. Applicable reuse terms remain unresolved.

unbundled_leads.title: The Book of Clement from the Ethiopian Bible: The First English Translation of Peter’s Visions Given to Clement
unbundled_leads.scope_description: Metadata-only discovery lead for the 2024 print edition. The retailer title/subtitle and secondary-project description associate the volume with Ethiopic Clement, but the volume itself was not inspected. The Geʽez base witness, translation path, textual boundaries, completeness, and accuracy are not established. The publisher's separate 2026 article describes a forthcoming revised reader edition with a 12-chapter arrangement and says complete Books V–VII fall outside that announced edition; do not assume this description applies to the 2024 book. Its identification with the scholarly Maṣḥafa Qalemǝnṭos (CAe 1957), the Ethiopic Apocalypse of Peter, or the exact work intended by the Church-list ‘Book of Clement’ remains unverified. Do not conflate it with 1 Clement or the three Epistles of Clement. No text is bundled.
unbundled_leads.rights_status: Retail availability is not a reuse grant. No open license or redistribution permission for the English translation or underlying text was identified; no text is bundled.

unbundled_leads.title: The Book of Clement from the Ethiopian Bible, Revised Reader’s Edition (announced; publication unconfirmed)
unbundled_leads.scope_description: Metadata-only announced edition. The publisher maps modern chapters 1–5 to manuscript Book I, 6–7 to Book II, 8–10 to Book III, and 11 to Book IV. It says chapter 12 follows a short summary of Books V and VII, and that the complete translation of Books V–VII lies outside the edition; the article's summarized-book wording is uneven and is preserved as reported. This is the publisher's description, not a checked text or a source-manuscript collation. The modern chapters are not established as Geʽez manuscript boundaries. The article does not establish the exact crosswalk to the Church-list entry or Bausi's CAe 1957 work. Publication is unconfirmed and no text is bundled.
unbundled_leads.rights_status: The publisher article does not grant reuse permission for the announced edition or underlying scripture. Publication and rights are unverified; no text is bundled.

unbundled_leads.title: Ethiopic Clement 6:83–86 — reported partial English rendering
unbundled_leads.scope_description: A 2025-11-05 Ethiopian Orthodox Bible Project announcement reports an English rendering of four verses (6:83–86) from a manuscript it describes as Amharic, supplemented by S. Grébaut's French translation. The announcement says verse 83 is rendered solely from French because the surviving Ethiopic is unintelligible. This is a publisher-reported, partial rendering, not a complete Clement reader; the exact source manuscript, French passage, edition, wording, and relation to the Church-list Book of Clement have not been independently verified. No text is bundled.
unbundled_leads.rights_status: Reuse rights for this modern English rendering are unknown. The project notice links to a commercial listing but grants no license to reproduce the text. No wording is copied.

entries.mapping_note: The Church list names Didascalia and Asale discusses it among broader-list additions. Platt 1834 and Harden 1920 are title-level candidate editions; their boundaries and relationship to the listed work have not been established. Gebru (2012, p. 29) describes a 43-chapter Ethiopic work with material beyond the Syriac Didascalia and reports Platt's English as partial (first 23 chapters); the report's textual-history interpretation and chapter numbering have not been checked against the witnesses. No verified reader text is bundled.

unbundled_leads.title: The Ethiopic Didascalia — Harden 1920, raw OCR research edition
unbundled_leads.scope_description: The source OCR is stored locally as unproofread TXT and page-structured XML. Harden's Introduction reports 43 chapters in four of five named manuscripts and says Platt's manuscript combines IV/V; this is a statement about the 1920 edition's reported witnesses. The OCR contains 43 main-text heading occurrences; all 43 headings were visually checked against the corresponding scan pages. The audit corrects OCR numeral errors on PDF pages 87 (X, OCR xX) and 165 (XXXI, OCR XXXII). Full text accuracy and scan completeness have not been reviewed. The relation to the Church-list Didascalia remains unverified. This is a source-access record, not a verified reader or canon crosswalk.
unbundled_leads.rights_status: The scanned volume's front matter states that there are no known copyright restrictions in the United States. The Arquivo Histórico da Igreja Lusitana lists a John Mason Harden as 1871–1931 (SRC-429), but this preliminary biographical record does not establish identity with this translator. These are source-reported leads, not an explicit open license or a global legal determination.

unbundled_leads.title: Didascalia apostolorum (EMML 675)
unbundled_leads.scope_description: The catalogue describes an Amharic introduction on fols. 1r–2r, then parallel Geʽez and Amharic columns, with 42 chapters and numbered paragraphs. It does not establish the exact boundaries or completeness of the Didascalia text in this codex, its relation to the Church-list entry “Didascalia,” or correspondence with any other edition. The link to eotc-nt-35 is a provisional title-level discovery candidate only; no reader text is bundled.
unbundled_leads.rights_status: HMML states partner institutions retain certain rights in digital images and prohibits image copying or redistribution without prior authorization; image access requires sign-in. Reuse rights for the manuscript transcription are not established. No text or images are copied.

unbundled_leads.title: The Ethiopic Didascalia — Platt 1834, TAU image edition
unbundled_leads.scope_description: The TAU menu exposes an introduction, 22 numbered sections (I–XXII), and notes as image-page selections. Only four image-page wrappers were sampled. Gebru (2012, printed p. 29) reports that Platt's English translation contains only the first 23 chapters of the 43-chapter Ethiopic work; this secondary report and TAU's 22 menu labels remain unreconciled. Neither describes a verified full extent or chapter crosswalk to the Church-list Didascalia. Raw IA OCR is stored separately for research, not as reader text.
unbundled_leads.rights_status: TAU grants noncommercial use, copying, and distribution of its digitized Ethiopic texts only with the stated Ran HaCohen copyright and permission notices; MDZ labels its scan ‘No Copyright - Non-Commercial Use Only’. This is conditional noncommercial permission, not an open or commercial license. QNL labels its catalogue object “No Known Copyright” but its disclaimer says third-party rights may apply and leaves reuse determinations to users. Image reuse and territory specific status remain to be reviewed; no verified text or images are bundled for this edition lead. A separate IA raw OCR capture is research-only.

unbundled_leads.title: The Ethiopic Didascalia — English translation accompanying Platt’s 1834 edition
unbundled_leads.scope_description: Partial English translation accompanying the 1834 Ethiopic edition. Gebru (2012, printed p. 29) reports that Platt's translation contains only the first 23 chapters of the 43-chapter Ethiopic Didascalia. TAU's menu labels I–XXII; the difference and the menu's relationship to printed chapters require examination. No English text is extracted or bundled, and the exact relation to the Church-list entry has not been established.
unbundled_leads.rights_status: MDZ labels the digitized volume ‘No Copyright - Non-Commercial Use Only’; TAU's permission for its digitized Ethiopic text requires noncommercial use and its stated notices. This is not an unrestricted or commercial license.

supplemental_research_views.source_name: Internet Archive — Harden 1920 Ethiopic Didascalia scan and raw OCR
supplemental_research_views.archive_status: Raw 1920 English OCR and source metadata stored offline for research; all 43 detected headings visually checked, with two OCR numeral errors corrected in the audit; no reader text or canon-linked coverage; public-domain claim scoped to the United States; translator identity and worldwide rights unresolved
supplemental_research_views.rights_status: The scanned book's front matter states that there are no known copyright restrictions in the United States. This is a US-scoped source claim, not a worldwide legal determination or a reuse license for the scan/OCR files. The Arquivo Histórico da Igreja Lusitana's preliminary authority record (SRC-429) lists a John Mason Harden as 1871–1931; this is a biographical lead only and identity with the translator is not established. The raw OCR remains unreviewed research material, not reader text.
supplemental_research_views.inspection_and_limitations: The Internet Archive item describes a Cornell University Library scan of J. M. Harden's The Ethiopic Didascalia, published in 1920, and its front matter states that there are no known copyright restrictions in the United States. Harden's Introduction (pp. xvii–xviii) says the known-complete Ethiopic work is divided into 43 chapters in four of five British Museum manuscripts; MS 798 and Platt's manuscript join chapters IV and V under one title. This is an edition-level report, not proof of the Church-list entry's chapter structure. The local OCR contains 43 main-text chapter-heading occurrences. The raw Tesseract TXT and XML OCR are retained byte-for-byte; their MD5/SHA-1 values match the provider metadata and their local SHA-256 values are recorded in the capture manifest. The TXT is not proofread, and the XML has 238 image objects. Visual checks of scan PDF pages 87, 165, and 169 show the printed headings CHAPTER X, CHAPTER XXXI, and CHAPTER XXXII; the OCR misreads the first two as XX and XXXII. All 43 detected headings were visually collated, and the structured audit is stored locally. This does not verify a complete text or every manuscript's chapter boundaries. OCR is not a verified reader, translation accuracy is not assessed, the catalogued scan does not establish global rights, and exact identity with the Church-list Didascalia is unresolved.
